title: Extreme poverty, conflict, displacement, and weak recovery are concentrating in high-fragility contexts with limited capacity to absorb shocks
source_unit: OECD, States of Fragility 2025, chapter on the state of fragility in 2025
geography: 177 global contexts assessed by the OECD multidimensional fragility framework, with detailed attention to 43 high-fragility and 18 extreme-fragility contexts

denominator.unit: global contexts analyzed by the OECD multidimensional fragility framework

high_fragility_contexts.unit: contexts identified as experiencing high fragility

extreme_fragility_contexts.unit: contexts identified as experiencing extreme fragility

population_in_high_extreme.unit: percent of the world population living in high- or extreme-fragility contexts

extreme_poverty_concentration.unit: percent of the world’s extreme poor living in high- or extreme-fragility contexts in 2024

observations.method: OECD multidimensional fragility framework covering political, security, economic, environmental, societal, and human dimensions across 177 contexts.
observations.uncertainty: Fragility is a multidimensional classification rather than a single causal variable; context boundaries, data coverage, and thresholds shape estimates and do not describe every locality or household.
observations.subgroup: Populations in high- and extreme-fragility contexts, extreme-poor households, governments, communities exposed to conflict, and people with unequal access to services and security.
observations.counterinterpretation: High fragility is not a permanent identity: some contexts have reduced exposure since 2015, and institutional reform, social cohesion, peacebuilding, and service delivery can change trajectories.

denominator.unit: global extreme-poverty projection under OECD fragility scenarios

extreme_poor_2040_projection.unit: percent of the world’s extreme poor potentially living in high- or extreme-fragility contexts by 2040

median_per_capita_growth_high_fragility.unit: percent median per-capita growth stabilizing in high-fragility contexts

median_per_capita_growth_extreme_fragili.unit: median per-capita growth pattern in extreme-fragility contexts

poverty_security_link.value: fragility, poverty, inequality, food insecurity, and forced displacement reinforce one another

observations.method: OECD projections and comparative analysis of fragility, extreme poverty, growth, inequality, food insecurity, and displacement.
observations.uncertainty: The 2040 figure is a projection contingent on demographic, conflict, growth, policy, and classification assumptions; it is not a forecast of inevitable geographic concentration.
observations.subgroup: Extreme-poor populations, high- and extreme-fragility contexts, low-income and middle-income countries, and public systems recovering from conflict and crisis.
observations.counterinterpretation: Targeted development, peacebuilding, social protection, inclusive growth, and institutional recovery can shift projected poverty concentration; low growth averages conceal successful local and national reforms.

denominator.unit: high- and extreme-fragility contexts identified by the OECD

organized_violence_contexts.unit: high- or extreme-fragility contexts affected by organized violence in 2023

forcibly_displaced_origin_host.unit: refugees and internally displaced persons originating in high- or extreme-fragility contexts, approximately

fdi_share.unit: percent or less of global net foreign-direct-investment inflows received by high- and extreme-fragility contexts in 2023

recovery_constraint.value: fragile contexts face simultaneous security, financing, governance, and service-delivery constraints

observations.method: OECD analysis of organized violence, forced displacement, foreign direct investment, economic recovery, and multidimensional fragility.
observations.uncertainty: Displacement and FDI measures use different sources and definitions; low FDI may reflect conflict, market size, risk, data, or other conditions rather than fragility alone.
observations.subgroup: Conflict-affected communities, refugees, internally displaced people, host communities, investors, governments, and service providers in fragile contexts.
observations.counterinterpretation: External finance is not the only route to recovery; domestic resource mobilization, diaspora transfers, local enterprise, public institutions, and peace agreements can matter substantially.

denominator.unit: high- and extreme-fragility contexts in the OECD framework

widest_gender_gap_contexts.unit: of the 10 contexts with the widest gender gaps exposed to high or extreme fragility

sdg_progress.value: no high- or extreme-fragility context is on track to achieve critical SDGs related to peace, hunger, health, and gender equality

policy_delivery.value: safety nets, rural development, gender-income-gap reduction, and equitable revenue generation depend on navigating combinations of fragility

fragility_dynamic.value: fragility should be treated as a dynamic risk and resilience spectrum rather than a fixed label

observations.method: OECD multidimensional analysis of gender equality, violence, democratic backsliding, SDG progress, policy delivery, and fragility combinations.
observations.uncertainty: Context-level associations do not show that fragility caused a specific gender or SDG outcome; institutional quality, conflict history, social norms, and data availability vary widely.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, marginalized groups, public institutions, civil society, safety-net users, and communities facing overlapping political, economic, security, and societal risks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Gender-responsive institutions and inclusive service delivery can be sources of resilience; worsening indicators are not proof that reform is impossible.

related_sources.claim: World Bank 2026 fragility-and-poverty reproducibility package provides a complementary extreme-poverty concentration route.
Official OECD States of Fragility 2025 publication landing page and framework context.
Official OECD chapter containing the fragility, poverty, displacement, finance, gender, and SDG findings.

boundary: This record adds a fragility-to-poverty concentration and state-capacity route linking conflict, inequality, food insecurity, displacement, FDI, gender, SDG progress, and policy delivery. It is not a household poverty survey, a causal conflict estimate, a forecast of any individual’s welfare, or respondent-level microdata analysis.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD States of Fragility 2025 chapter and publication pages were reviewed; context counts, population and poverty concentration, 2040 projection, displacement, FDI, gender, SDG, and dynamic-fragility claims were cross-checked.
